subject: Trial observability: evaluation plan, dashboards & next steps
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Elena Parks <elena.parks@tempodata.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2026 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Trial observability: evaluation plan, dashboards & next steps

Hi Elena —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before we spin up the trial environment: 

High-level trial goals (from today's call):
- Validate end-to-end inference latency under your baseline traffic (peak: ~180 qps).
- Verify end-to-end tracing/correlation (client request -> Redwood -> model -> response).
- Confirm retention and export of request/response logs to your S3 for downstream analytics.

Proposed success criteria (draft):
- 95th percentile inference latency <= 220ms for 0-512 token requests.
- All customer request IDs traceable across Redwood logs and spans for >= 99% of requests.
- Logs exported to S3 within 10 minutes for 100% of successful requests.
- No data leakage: only hashed IDs in logs; PII scrubber verified by your security team.

Observability deliverables Redwood will provide during the POC:
- A set of Kibana/Grafana dashboards (latency, throughput, error rates, model fallback events).
- Distributed tracing and a sample span schema that maps to your trace ids.
- Automatic log export to your S3 bucket + a short retention/config doc.

Immediate next steps: 
1) TempoData confirms success criteria above or sends edits by EOD Monday (6/29).
2) We (Redwood) will provision a trial instance and a shared dashboard workspace once we have the S3 write role and sample traffic pattern (see attachments).
3) Marissa will own the onboarding runbook and perform the initial smoke test. Jordan will own the tracing schema and metric mapping. I will coordinate the kickoff.

Attachments: POC checklist and sample dashboards (stubs below).

If that looks good, can you confirm resources (S3 bucket + IAM role) and the preferred kickoff window next week?

Thanks — Rafael
Rafael Mendes
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference

[Attachment: Tempodata-POC-Eval-Checklist.xlsx (xlsx)]
[Attachment: mutual-action-plan-TempoData.pdf (pdf)]

From: Elena Parks <elena.parks@tempodata.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Cc: Matt Li <matt.li@tempodata.com>
Date: Sat, 26 Jun 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Trial observability: evaluation plan, dashboards & next steps

Rafael —

Appreciate the write-up, this is really helpful. A few clarifications from our side: 

Success criteria tweaks:
- Can we tighten the latency SLO to p95 <= 200ms for small payloads (<128 tokens)? For larger payloads you can keep the 220ms cap.
- Tracing: we need end-to-end sampling at 100% for the POC window (we can relax after evaluation).
- Logs: export to S3 within 15 minutes is acceptable for the first 72 hours while we tune ingestion.

I will confirm IAM role and a dedicated S3 prefix by Monday morning. Matt will be the primary technical contact for the integration work and will join the kickoff.

Kickoff preference: Tue 7/6 or Wed 7/7 in the morning PT.

Thanks — Elena
Elena Parks
Director, Platform Engineering | TempoData

Jordan/Marissa —

Elena pushed for tighter p95 for small payloads and 100% tracing sampling for the POC window. Can you both own the following?

Ownership: 
- Jordan: tracing/span schema + example trace IDs mapping to TempoData request IDs. Deliverable: trace-schema.json + 3 sample traces. Target: 7/2 EOD.
- Marissa: dashboard pack + onboarding runbook. Deliverable: shared dashboard links + smoke test checklist. Target: 7/3 EOD.

Observability scope suggestions (what we should stand up for the trial):
- Dashboards:
  * Inference latency (p50/p95/p99) by model variant and token bucket
  * Throughput (RPS) and concurrent requests
  * Error breakdown (model timeouts, infra throttles, bad inputs)
  * Fallback events (when we route to a cheaper model)
- Tracing: request.id -> span.id -> model-call span; include metadata tags: tenant_id, route, model_version, token_count
- Logs: request/response logs (redacted) + export to S3; retention policy during trial: 14 days in Redwood, full export kept to your S3

I'll compile the deliverables into the HubSpot record and link the Drive folder. Rafael, please confirm whether 7/6 kickoff works with TempoData.

— Jordan (cc'd) and Marissa (cc'd)

Subject: Re: Trial observability: evaluation plan, dashboards & next steps

Elena —

Quick note on mapping Redwood metrics to TempoData acceptance criteria so there's no ambiguity during verification: 

- Latency: p95 <= 200ms for token_count < 128 -> Redwood metric: inference.latency.ms (percentile, filter token_count:<128)
- Tracing: sampling=100% -> Redwood tracing.sampling set to 1.0 for tempo-poc namespace; we will emit a trace header x-trace-id that matches your x-correlation-id
- Log export: export_success.latency.ms -> we will alert if any export takes > 900 seconds (15 minutes) and keep an export retry counter visible on dashboard

Deliverables attached: sample trace snippets and a JSON export of our sample Kibana view (small stub attached). Also linking a short smoke test plan we will run during the first 2 hours of the kickoff.

Notes: We will keep sampling at 100% only for the trial namespace; no change to tenant-level defaults.

Regards,
Jordan
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

[Attachment: redwood-sample-kibana-views.json (json)]

Elena/Rafael —

I've placed a preliminary dashboard pack in the shared Drive (link below) and attached the onboarding runbook. Key items I will execute during kickoff: 

Kickoff smoke tests (owner: Marissa):
- Validate API keys & routing for the tempo-poc namespace
- Send 1k synthetic requests at your baseline distribution (we'll run small/med/large token mixes)
- Confirm traces for 100% of requests and look up 10 sample request IDs end-to-end
- Confirm S3 export into the tempo-poc prefix and verify file manifests

Escalation path: If any step fails, I'll escalate to our infra on-call and loop Rafael.

Target timeline:
- 7/2: deliver dashboard pack and runbook (done)
- 7/3: internal smoke run in our staging to sanity-check dashboards
- 7/6: customer kickoff and live smoke run
